grammarFocus: 第一、第二条件句的常见用途；建议与可能性的表达。
title: The Community Garden Project
instructions: 阅读下面的文章，回答10个问题。文章是关于社区服务与问题解决的。请仔细阅读，然后完成选择题、填空题和判断题。判断题请选择 True、False 或 Not Given。所有答案必须来自文章。本材料为模拟练习，不是官方雅思考试。
passage:
When the local council announced plans to sell a small piece of land near the town centre, residents of Millbrook were worried. The land had been unused for years, but it was the only green space in the area. A group of neighbours decided to take action. They formed a committee and proposed turning the land into a community garden. The council agreed to rent the land to the community for a small fee, on the condition that the garden would be open to everyone.

The committee faced several challenges. First, the land was covered in rubbish and weeds. Volunteers spent three weekends clearing it. Second, they needed funding for tools, seeds, and a water supply. They applied for a small grant from a local charity and organised a fundraising event. The event raised enough money to buy basic equipment. Third, some residents worried that the garden would attract noise and litter. The committee held a public meeting to listen to these concerns and promised to set clear rules about opening hours and rubbish disposal.

Work on the garden began in spring. Volunteers built raised beds, planted vegetables and flowers, and installed a compost bin. They also created a small play area for children. The garden quickly became a popular place. People from different backgrounds met and worked together. Older residents shared gardening tips with younger ones, and children learned where food comes from.

However, problems soon appeared. Some teenagers started using the garden at night, and there were complaints about broken bottles and noise. The committee discussed possible solutions. One suggestion was to lock the garden at dusk, but some members argued that this would prevent people from enjoying the garden in the evening. Another idea was to install lighting, but that would be expensive. Finally, they decided to set up a volunteer rota so that someone would be present in the evenings. They also organised activities for teenagers, such as a weekly gardening club, to give them a sense of ownership.

These measures worked well. The vandalism stopped, and the garden became even more popular. The committee now runs workshops on composting and water saving. They also share surplus vegetables with a local food bank. The project has brought the community closer together. As one volunteer said, "If we hadn't worked together, none of this would have happened."

The garden is now in its third year. The committee is planning to expand it by taking over an adjacent plot. They have applied for further funding and are confident about the future. They believe that if more people get involved, the garden will continue to grow and benefit the whole community. In addition, the committee has started a monthly newsletter to keep residents informed about events and volunteer opportunities. They hope that this will encourage more people to join. The garden also hosts school visits, where children learn about growing food and looking after the environment. The committee is proud of what they have achieved and is eager to share their experience with other communities. They have even received requests from neighbouring areas for advice on starting similar projects. The garden has become a model for community-led urban green spaces. The committee also plans to hold a celebration event next month to thank all the volunteers and to mark the garden's third anniversary. They will invite local businesses to support the event and hope to attract new volunteers. The event will include a plant sale, a children's art competition, and a guided tour of the garden. The committee believes that such events help to strengthen community bonds and raise awareness of the garden's benefits. They are also considering starting a 'friends of the garden' scheme, where residents can make a small monthly donation to support the garden's upkeep. This would provide a steady income and reduce reliance on grants. The committee is keen to hear residents' ideas and will discuss these proposals at the next public meeting.

questions.prompt: What was the council's original plan for the land?
options: To turn it into a car park
To give it to the community

questions.prompt: What condition did the council set for renting the land to the community?
options: The garden must be open to everyone.
The community must pay a large fee.
The garden must be finished within a year.
The community must employ a gardener.
answers: The garden must be open to everyone.

questions.prompt: How many weekends did volunteers spend clearing the land? (Use a number.)

questions.evidence: Volunteers spent three weekends clearing it.

questions.prompt: How did the committee raise money for tools and seeds?
options: By applying for a grant and organising a fundraising event
By asking the council for money
answers: By applying for a grant and organising a fundraising event

questions.prompt: What was one concern raised by some residents?

The garden would be too expensive.

options: They held a public meeting and set clear rules.

questions.explanation: 第二段最后提到 'The committee held a public meeting to listen to these concerns and promised to set clear rules about opening hours and rubbish disposal.'，所以是召开公开会议并制定明确规则。
questions.evidence: The committee held a public meeting to listen to these concerns and promised to set clear rules about opening hours and rubbish disposal.

The water supply was cut off.
The council took back the land.
answers: Teenagers used the garden at night and caused damage.

options: Setting up a volunteer rota and organising activities for teenagers

grammar.title: 第一、第二条件句的常见用途；建议与可能性的表达
grammar.explanation: 第一条件句（if + 一般现在时，主句用 will/can/may + 动词原形）表示很可能发生的情况及其结果。第二条件句（if + 一般过去时，主句用 would/could/might + 动词原形）表示假设的、不太可能或与现在事实相反的情况。建议可以用 'should'、'why don't we...?'、'how about...?' 等表达。可能性可以用 'may'、'might'、'could' 等表达。
grammar.example: If we hadn't worked together, none of this would have happened.

questions.prompt: If it rains tomorrow, we ______ the gardening workshop.
questions.explanation: 第一条件句表示将来可能发生的情况，主句用 will + 动词原形。

questions.prompt: If I were you, I ______ more volunteers.
questions.explanation: 第二条件句表示假设，主句用 would + 动词原形。

options: Why don't we plant more trees?
answers: Why don't we plant more trees?
questions.explanation: 'Why don't we...?' 是提出建议的常用句型。
